description:
Sites:
- crate-jmap-mail-server/src/email.rs:1562-1566   — receivedAt from client on Email/set create
- crate-jmap-calendars-server/src/principal.rs:46-56  — utcStart, utcEnd from client on Principal/getAvailability

Both use `obj_val.get(field).and_then(|v| v.as_str()).map(UTCDate::from)` against client-supplied wire input. `UTCDate::from` is infallible and accepts any String, so malformed timestamps flow into downstream string compares with undefined ordering behaviour.

The canonical fix pattern was just landed for jmap-chat-server in commit 533ee8a (closing JMAP-g7wu.9.11 and the JMAP-g7wu.9 epic):

```rust
match UTCDate::new_validated(s) {
    Ok(d) => { /* use d */ }
    Err(_) => {
        not_created.insert(
            create_id.clone(),
            json!({ "type": "invalidProperties", "properties": [field_name] }),
        );
        continue;
    }
}
```

That fix was applied to all three chat-server wire boundaries (ban.rs, invite.rs, message.rs) but did NOT propagate to the sibling extension-server crates per the cookie-cutter rule in workspace AGENTS.md ("If you change this crate, propagate the change to every extension-server sibling in the same pass"). The JMAP-g7wu.9 epic was closed marking the workspace-wide migration complete despite this gap.

Why P2 (not P1): unvalidated dates flow through but the impact is bounded — string compares produce undefined ordering, not crashes. Calendars-server availability queries with malformed input would return arbitrary windows. Mail-server email/set with malformed receivedAt would store a bogus timestamp and subsequent sort/filter by receivedAt would return arbitrary ordering. Defensible as P2: client error producing wrong-but-bounded results, not P1 silent data loss or panic.

Why idiomatic-rust: the entire point of `new_validated` returning `Result<UTCDate, ParseError>` is to push validation to the wire boundary. Using `.from()` (infallible) on client-supplied input defeats the type-system intent.

Sibling check via `rg 'UTCDate::from\(' crate-jmap-*-server/src/`:
- mail-server: 1 client-boundary site (email.rs:1562)
- calendars-server: 2 client-boundary sites (principal.rs:49, principal.rs:55)
- chat-server: 0 client-boundary sites remaining (all migrated)
- tasks/contacts/filenode/sharing-server: 0 sites with client-supplied UTCDate
- Server-internal sites that consume `now_utc_string()` are not affected — those values are well-formed by construction.

Note: a partial mitigation is that the wire parsing in jmap-types::UTCDate is currently lossy by design (no validation in `from`), so even a fully validated boundary needs the `UTCDate::new_validated` ladder; `UTCDate::from` alone is not the answer.
title: P2: UTCDate boundary validation gap — chat-server fixed, mail-server & calendars-server still unvalidated
